title: P N Gadgil Jewellers Ltd - 544256 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR10,739 crore, with full-year gross margin up 280 bps to 12% and EBITDA margin up 180 bps to 6.6%. Q4 revenue grew 123% YoY to INR3,544 crore, but gross margin fell to 9.7% (about 230 bps down YoY) as gold bars and coins rose to 40% of sales, plus one-time discounts and franchise mix. Management attributes the Q4 margin dip to mix and one-offs, and it guided FY27 revenue of INR13,500 crore, EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%, with a review next quarter given the import duty hike.

financial_highlights.change: about -230 bps YoY; gross profit +80% YoY

segments.name: Retail (COCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 retail revenue INR8,131 crore (+51% YoY), SSSG 43%; Q4 retail INR2,600 crore (+102% YoY). Stud ratio for FY26 at 9.9%.

segments.name: Franchise (FOCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 franchise revenue INR1,292 crore (+83% YoY); Q4 INR430 crore (+132% YoY). Franchise gross margin cited at 2.5-3%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR529 crore (+105% YoY); Q4 INR152 crore (+67% YoY).

segments.name: Other segments
segments.commentary: Q4 contribution INR357 crore; includes gold bars and coins, which carry roughly 0.5-1% gross margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR13,500 crore, versus the earlier INR12,000-12,500 crore reference; retail AOP about INR9,800 crore (+23% on about INR8,000 crore).
FY27 EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin about 4%; gross margin guidance 12-13%, which management says is unchanged.
Guidance to be updated next quarter depending on how market conditions evolve.
Bars and coins expected at about 25% of sales in FY27 (FY26: about 32%); the import duty hike is expected to cut that segment by 20-22% of total sales.
FY27 store plan of 25 new stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO (about 20 franchise), mostly outside Maharashtra (Gurgaon, Lucknow/UP, Gujarat).
Hedging target raised to 75-80% in FY27 (67% at end-Q4 FY26, about 60% average for FY26).
capex_capacity: 78 stores across 36 cities at 31 March 2026; 25 stores added in FY26, including 12 in Q4 (8 COCO, 4 FOCO).
Non-Maharashtra stores contribute about 10% of business; UP, Bihar and MP stores reached about 1x annualised stock turn in year one, against a 0.8x guidance.
Average revenue per store INR137.7 crore; revenue per sq ft INR4,51,000; net profit per store INR5.25 crore; inventory turnover 3.8x.
Management says it does not plan many COCO stores in FY27, favouring the asset-light franchise model.
QIP enabling board resolution valid until end of August 2026; management says the QIP is not needed for growth. Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027.
demand_pricing: Q4 event sales: Foundation Day INR365 crore, Gudi Padwa INR171 crore (+38% YoY), Gratitude Day INR225 crore.
Q4 volumes: gold +27% YoY, silver +37%, diamond +125%, despite a sharp gold price run.
Old gold exchange about 40% of business, targeted at 50%+; make-to-order about 30-35% (22% outside Maharashtra vs 30-32% in Maharashtra).
Average transaction value above INR1 lakh in FY26.

Q4 gross margin hit by about 150 bps from bars and coins (INR450 crore to INR1,400 crore; Q3 INR1,100 crore), about 100 bps from lower stud mix, and INR40-45 crore of making-charge discounts (INR399/gram), plus INR50 crore+ of promotional and trade discounts. Franchise sales rose about INR200 crore QoQ.
Gains from the unhedged portion: INR7.4 crore in Q4 FY25, INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26.
Management says the import duty and the advance authorisation scheme do not apply to its domestic business; the duty is passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

risks_watch: Q4 gross margin at 9.7% versus 12-13% guidance; management says the mix shift will normalise, but its explanation of one-offs has been challenged.
Import duty hike may reduce bars and coins demand (20-22% of sales); whether jewellery exchange offsets it is unproven, and management said it is too early to quantify FY27 volume.
Hedging at 67% is short of the 75-80% target; MCX margin costs and unhedged gains affect margin volatility.
Franchise mix rising (FOCO margins about 2-3%) could weigh on gross margin as the network expands.
Inventory turnover fell to 3.8x as new stores ramp; the new-market ramp needs watching.
Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027; the QIP enabling resolution lapses end-August 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year result and the FY27 guidance, but defensive on Q4 margins: management repeatedly ties the drop to bars and coins and one-off promotions and says it is not structural. It was less specific on FY27 volume, the QIP and hedging costs, and said it would update guidance next quarter.
key_quotes: So, the three factors primarily which can identify to this are higher share of gold bars and coins in the overall sales mix.
We therefore view the gross margin impact as largely one-time and mix-driven, not structural, and remain focused on improving product mix and margins as our stores mature.
So, we feel looking at these positives, you know, we feel that INR12,500 can be stretched to INR13,500, and that's where the guidance is coming from.
